text: 3M Company, incorporated in 1929 under the laws of the State of Delaware, filed an annual report on Form 10-K with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2018, under Commission file number 1-3285. The company’s principal executive offices are located at 3M Center, St. Paul, Minnesota 55144, and its ticker symbol is MMM. The report includes information on the company’s securities, which are registered on the New York Stock Exchange, Inc., including Common Stock, Par Value $.01 Per Share, and various notes such as 1.500% Notes due 2026, Floating Rate Notes due 2020, 0.375% Notes due 2022, 0.950% Notes due 2023, 1.750% Notes due 2030, and 1.500% Notes due 2031. The common stock is also traded on the SWX Swiss Exchange. As of January 31, 2019, the aggregate market value of voting stock held by nonaffiliates was approximately $115.3 billion, with 575.8 million shares of common stock outstanding. The company operates in five business segments: Industrial, Safety and Graphics, Health Care, Electronics and Energy, and Consumer. At December 31, 2018, 3M employed 93,516 people, including 37,412 in the United States and 56,104 internationally. The Industrial segment serves markets such as automotive OEM and aftermarket, electronics, appliance, packaging, food and beverage, and construction, offering products like tapes, adhesives, sealants, filtration products, and advanced ceramics. In 2016, 3M sold its pressurized polyurethane foam adhesives and adhesive-backed temporary protective films businesses; in 2018, it divested a polymer additives compounding business and an abrasives glass products business. The Safety and Graphics segment provides personal protection products, commercial graphics, transportation safety solutions, and roofing granules, having acquired Scott Safety in October 2017 and sold its safety prescription eyewear business in January 2017 and certain personal safety product offerings in February 2018. The Health Care segment serves medical clinics, hospitals, pharmaceuticals, dental practitioners, and food manufacturing, offering medical tapes, dressings, wound care products, surgical supplies, drug delivery systems, and oral care solutions. The report is filed pursuant to Section 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and the company is a well-known seasoned issuer, not required to file reports under Section 13 or 15(d), and has submitted electronically all required Interactive Data Files. The document incorporates by reference certain parts of the company’s definitive proxy statement for its annual meeting on May 14, 2019, including Items 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14 of Part III.

3M operates in three main business segments: Health Care, Electronics and Energy, and Consumer. In the Health Care segment, 3M serves markets including medical clinics, hospitals, pharmaceuticals, dental and orthodontic practitioners, health information systems, and food manufacturing and testing. Products include medical tapes, dressings, wound closure products, orthopedic casting materials, acute wound care, skin integrity and disinfecting port protection, surgical drapes, masks, preps, electrodes, stethoscopes, sterilization assurance equipment, patient warming solutions, drug delivery systems such as metered-dose inhalers and transdermal patches, oral care solutions like restoratives, adhesives, crowns, impression materials, preventive sealants, professional tooth whiteners, prophylaxis, orthodontic appliances, and digital workflow solutions, as well as health information systems software for hospital coding and data classification. In September 2017, 3M purchased Elution Technologies, LLC, a Vermont-based manufacturer of test kits that help food and beverage companies detect allergens such as peanuts, soy, or milk. The Electronics and Energy segment serves customers in electronics and energy markets, offering solutions that improve the dependability, cost-effectiveness, and performance of electronic devices, electrical products including infrastructure protection, and power generation and distribution. This segment provides display materials and systems, including films for LCD computer monitors, LCD televisions, handheld devices, notebook PCs, and automotive displays, as well as screen filters for light control, privacy, and glare reduction. It also offers packaging and interconnection devices, high-performance fluids and abrasives for computer chip manufacturing and cooling, high-temperature and display tapes, flexible circuits used in ink-jet printers, cell phones, and electronic devices, and touch systems including touch screens and sensors. In December 2016, 3M sold the assets of its cathode battery technology out-licensing business. Energy solutions include electrical infrastructure protection, renewable energy components for solar and wind power, and infrastructure protection and detection solutions for electrical, oil, natural gas, water, rebar, and other assets. In June 2018, 3M completed the sale of substantially all of its Communication Markets Division, with the remaining telecommunications systems services portion based in Germany sold in December 2018. The Consumer segment serves markets such as consumer retail, online retail, office retail, office business to business, home improvement, drug and pharmacy retail, and other markets. Major consumer products include Scotch® brand items like Scotch® Magic™ Tape, Scotch® Glue Stick, Scotch® Cushioned Mailer, Post-it® Products such as Post-it® Flags, Post-it® Extreme Notes, Post-it® Note Pads, Post-it® Labeling & Cover-up Tape, and Post-it® Pop-up Notes and Dispensers, home improvement products like ScotchBlue™ painter tapes, surface-preparation and wood-finishing materials, Command™ Adhesive Products, Filtrete™ Filters and Room Air Purifiers, home care products such as Scotch-Brite® Scour Pads, Scotch-Brite® Scrub Sponges, Scotch-Brite® Microfiber Cloth products, O-Cel-O™ Sponges, protective materials like Scotchgard™ Fabric Protectors, maintenance-free respirators, personal safety products including safety glasses, hearing protectors, and 3M Thinsulate™ Insulation used in warm clothing, as well as Nexcare™ Adhesive Bandages and ACE® branded elastic bandages, supports, and thermometers. 3M sells its products globally through direct sales and various distribution channels including wholesalers, retailers, jobbers, distributors, and dealers. Research and development expenses totaled $1.821 billion in 2018, $1.870 billion in 2017, and $1.764 billion in 2016, with $1.253 billion in 2018 related to basic scientific research and product development. The company owns or holds licenses to numerous U.S. and foreign patents, which provide a competitive advantage, though no single patent is essential to any business segment. In 2018, 3M spent approximately $27 million on environmental capital projects, excluding remediation costs for past operations, which are expensed. These projects include pollution control devices such as wastewater treatment improvements, scrubbers, containment structures, solvent recovery units, and thermal oxidizers. The company expects approximately $75 million in capital expenditures over the next two years for new or expanded environmental programs to reduce waste and emissions. 3M’s manufacturing operations are subject to environmental laws worldwide, and the company makes necessary expenditures for compliance and remediation at certain sites. In 2018, raw material prices increased globally, but 3M mitigated impacts through productivity projects, input management, reformulations, and multi-sourcing, maintaining sufficient raw material supplies. The Company provides information on the scope, nature, or impact of acquisition, strategic alliance, and divestiture activities, the outcome of legal and regulatory proceedings, future levels of indebtedness, common stock repurchases, and capital spending, future availability of and access to credit markets, pension and postretirement obligation assumptions and future contributions, asset impairments, tax liabilities, information technology security, and the effects of changes in tax laws (including the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act), environmental and other laws and regulations in the United States and other countries where it operates. The Company operates in more than 70 countries and derives approximately 60 percent of its revenues from outside the United States, making it subject to global competition, geopolitical risks, economic downturns, inflation, unemployment, trade restrictions, natural disasters, and changes in capital availability or exchange rates. The Company’s credit ratings, currently AA- with a stable outlook from Standard & Poor’s and A1 with a stable outlook from Moody’s, influence its cost of capital and access to lenders; increased leverage could negatively impact these ratings. Competitive conditions, customer preferences, and the timing and market acceptance of new product offerings affect revenue and profit margins, with risks related to product development, intellectual property, and market acceptance. Fluctuations in the cost and availability of raw materials, components, and energy, including oil and natural gas, due to supply disruptions or currency risks, could materially affect operations. Acquisitions, strategic alliances, divestitures, and organizational restructuring may affect future results, with integration and synergy realization being key factors. Productivity improvements through Lean Six Sigma and business transformation, including the phased global implementation of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, are expected but not guaranteed. Information technology security risks, including cyberattacks, system failures, and data breaches, could disrupt operations, compromise data, and damage reputation, despite existing cybersecurity measures and insurance. The Company’s defined benefit pension and postretirement plans are exposed to financial market risks, such as interest rate changes and investment losses, which could increase funding obligations. Legal and regulatory proceedings, including product liability, antitrust, intellectual property, environmental, and anti-bribery matters, carry uncertainty in outcomes and could result in material charges. In the United States, 3M’s general offices, corporate research laboratories, and certain division laboratories are located in St. Paul, Minnesota, and it operates 75 manufacturing facilities in 29 U.S. states and 107 manufacturing and converting facilities in 36 countries internationally, owning the majority of its physical properties. As of January 31, 2019, there were 76,596 shareholders of record; 3M’s stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), Chicago Stock Exchange, and SWX Swiss Exchange under the ticker symbol MMM. Cash dividends totaled $1.36 and $1.175 per share for each quarter in 2018 and 2017, respectively. The Company’s Board of Directors authorized a $10 billion common stock repurchase program in February 2016, which was replaced in November 2018 with a new program authorizing up to $10 billion of repurchases with no pre-established end date. Total common stock repurchases from January 1 to December 31, 2018, amounted to 23,289,158 shares at an average price of $207.46, with total expenditures of $9,396 million. In 2018, cash dividends declared and paid totaled $1.36 per share for each quarter, with dividends typically declared and paid in the same quarter. In December 2014, 3M declared dividends that were paid in the following first quarter. For the fourth quarter of 2018, net income attributable to 3M was $1.347 billion, or $2.27 per diluted share, compared to $523 million, or $0.85 per diluted share, in the same quarter of 2017, an increase of 167 percent on a per diluted share basis. Adjusting for the Minnesota natural resource damages (NRD) resolution and the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) measurement period adjustment, net income was $1.366 billion, or $2.31 per diluted share, compared to $1.285 billion, or $2.10 per diluted share, in the fourth quarter of 2017, an increase of 10.0 percent. For the full year 2018, net income attributable to 3M was $5.349 billion, or $8.89 per diluted share, compared to $4.858 billion, or $7.93 per diluted share, in 2017, an increase of 12.1 percent. Adjusting for the NRD matter and TCJA, net income was $6.295 billion, or $10.46 per diluted share, compared to $5.620 billion, or $9.17 per diluted share, in 2017, an increase of 14.1 percent. In May 2017, 3M completed the divestiture of its identity management business, reflecting a pre-tax gain of $457 million, which was reported within the Safety and Graphics business. In June 2018, 3M completed the sale of substantially all of its Communication Markets Division, reflecting a pre-tax gain of $494 million, and in December 2018, sold the remaining telecommunications system integration services portion of the business in Germany, reflecting a pre-tax gain of $15 million, both reported within the Electronics and Energy business. During the second and fourth quarters of 2018, restructuring actions related to the Communication Markets Division divestiture affected approximately 1,200 positions worldwide, resulting in pre-tax charges of $105 million in the second quarter and $22 million in the fourth quarter. These actions increased earnings per diluted share by 2 cents and 50 cents, respectively. The effective tax rate for the fourth quarter of 2018 was 21.6 percent, a decrease of 47 percentage points from 2017, and for the full year 2018 was 23.4 percent, a decrease of 12.1 percentage points from 2017. Excluding the Minnesota NRD resolution and TCJA measurement period adjustment, the effective income tax rate was 20.5 percent in the fourth quarter and 20.1 percent for the full year. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily due to the favorable aspects of the TCJA, including the decrease in the U.S. income tax rate, foreign-derived intangible income (FDII), and increased benefits from the R&D tax credit, partially offset by the elimination of the domestic manufacturing deduction, the global intangible low-taxed income (GILTI) provision, and lower excess tax benefits from employee share-based payments. Lower shares outstanding increased earnings per share by 8 cents in the fourth quarter and 18 cents for the full year, due to a 3.4 percent and 1.8 percent year-on-year decline in weighted-average diluted shares outstanding, resulting from the Company’s purchase of $1.3 billion in the fourth quarter and $4.9 billion in the full year of 2018.

In the fourth quarter of 2018, 3M recorded a tax charge of $22 million, net of adjustments for reductions in cost estimates, and a full-year 2018 pre-tax charge of $105 million. The aggregate net impact of the gain on sale and related restructuring actions increased earnings per diluted share by 2 cents for the fourth quarter and 50 cents for the full year 2018, reflecting the specific income tax rate associated with these items. In May 2017, 3M completed the sale or transfer of control of its identity management business, reflecting a pre-tax gain of $457 million, with the earnings per share impact reflecting the specific income tax rate used for this divestiture. Organic growth and productivity in 2017 included benefits from higher organic local-currency sales, raw material cost decreases from sourcing cost reduction projects, and business transformation, partially offset by higher defined benefit pension service cost expenses, and were the primary drivers of year-on-year benefit. Year-on-year incremental strategic investments decreased pre-tax earnings by approximately $413 million, consisting of investments in growth initiatives and portfolio and supply chain optimization. Acquisitions and divestitures (other than the identity management business sale) had a neutral impact on earnings per diluted share for full year 2017; the acquisition of Scott Safety in the fourth quarter of 2017 resulted in a net year-on-year decrease of 7 cents per diluted share due to transaction and integration costs, offset by income from operations and financing costs. Divestitures in 2017, including Polyfoam and the library system business (first quarter 2016), protective films and cathode battery technology (fourth quarter 2016), prescription safety eyewear (January 2017), tolling and automated license/number plate recognition (second quarter 2017), and electronic monitoring (fourth quarter 2017), contributed to a year-on-year pre-tax gain increase of approximately 7 cents per diluted share. Foreign currency impacts (net of hedging) decreased pre-tax earnings by $111 million year-on-year, equivalent to a 13-cent decrease per diluted share. In the fourth quarter of 2017, 3M increased its accruals for respirator mask and asbestos liabilities. Other expense decreased earnings per share due to a $96 million loss on extinguishment of debt and higher interest rates, contributing to an 11-cent decrease per diluted share, and interest expenses from Scott Safety contributed a 2-cent decrease. Higher defined benefit and postretirement service cost expenses and defined contribution expenses, along with lower income from non-service cost components, increased expenses year-on-year. The effective income tax rate was 35.5 percent in 2017, an increase of 7.2 percentage points from 2016, with an effective rate of 25.4 percent excluding the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA), a 2.9 percentage point decrease. In February 2018, 3M reached a settlement with the State of Minnesota regarding the Natural Resource Damages (NRD) lawsuit, agreeing to provide an $850 million grant to establish a “3M Water Quality and Sustainability Fund” for water sustainability and habitat projects in the Twin Cities East Metro region. 3M recorded a $897 million charge in the first quarter of 2018, including legal fees, and a $60 million tax expense in the fourth quarter of 2018 related to IRS examination under the Compliance Assurance Process (CAP) and new TCJA guidance. A $217 million tax expense was recorded in the first quarter of 2018 for a measurement period adjustment to the provisional TCJA amounts from December 2017, and a $41 million reversal of previously recorded tax expense was finalized in the fourth quarter of 2018. In the fourth quarter of 2017, 3M recorded a $762 million net tax expense related to the TCJA, primarily due to the transition tax on previously unremitted earnings of non-U.S. subsidiaries, net of remeasurement of deferred tax assets and liabilities. The Company provides non-GAAP measures adjusted for the impacts of the NRD resolution and TCJA measurement period adjustments, which are not substitutes for GAAP measures but are used to evaluate underlying operating trends. For the fourth quarter of 2018, adjusted non-GAAP measures showed operating income of $1,783 million, net income of $1,366 million, and earnings per diluted share of $2.31, compared to $1,789 million, $1,347 million, and $2.27 in the fourth quarter of 2017. For the full year 2018, adjusted non-GAAP measures showed operating income of $8,104 million, net income of $6,295 million, and earnings per diluted share of $10.46, compared to $7,692 million, $5,620 million, and $9.17 in 2017. In the fourth quarter of 2018, total company sales were $7,945 million, down 0.6 percent from $7,990 million in 2017, with operating income of $1,783 million, down 0.3 percent from $1,789 million. Sales and operating income by segment showed Industrial sales at $2,952 million (37.2% of total), Safety and Graphics at $1,569 million (19.8%), Health Care at $1,520 million (19.1%), Electronics and Energy at $1,342 million (16.9%), and Consumer at $1,211 million (15.2%). Industrial sales decreased 0.3 percent with organic local-currency sales growth of 2.5 percent, operating income margins at 21.2 percent, up 1.6 percentage points. Safety and Graphics sales increased 0.3 percent on an organic local-currency basis of 3.3 percent, operating income margins at 22.0 percent, down 3.9 percentage points. Health Care sales increased 2.4 percent on an organic local-currency basis of 4.8 percent, operating income margins at 30.2 percent, down 0.8 percentage points. Electronics and Energy sales decreased 4.5 percent with organic local-currency sales growth of 4.1 percent, operating income margins at 29.5 percent, up 3.5 percentage points. Consumer sales increased 0.1 percent on an organic local-currency basis of 1.9 percent, operating income margins at 21.3 percent, down 1.1 percentage points.

In 2018, 3M's total company sales were $32,765 million, up 3.5% from 2017, with operating income at $7,207 million, a decrease of 6.3% from 2017. By business segment, Industrial sales were $12,267 million, up 3.4% with operating income margins of 37.4% (up 0.9% from 2017), while Safety and Graphics sales were $6,827 million, up 9.5% with margins of 20.8% (up 1.1 percentage points), Health Care sales were $6,021 million, up 2.9% with margins of 18.4% (up 2.0 percentage points), Electronics and Energy sales were $5,472 million, down 0.5% with margins of 16.7% (up 3.5 percentage points, with 1.9 percentage points attributed to the divestiture of the Communication Markets Division), and Consumer sales were $4,796 million, up 1.4% with margins of 14.6% (down 2.4 percentage points). Operating income margins were 30.2% for the total company, down 0.8 percentage points. In Electronics and Energy, total sales decreased 4.5% while organic local currency sales increased 4.1%, with electronics-related sales increasing 2.1% (3.2% organically) and energy-related sales decreasing 22.7% while organic sales increased 4.5%, driven by growth in electrical markets. In Consumer, total sales increased 0.1% (1.9% organically), with growth in home improvement and stationery and office, while home care and consumer health care declined, and operating income margins were 21.3%, down 1.1 percentage points, including a 0.5 percentage point increase from 2017 portfolio and footprint actions not repeated in 2018. Geographically, Europe, Latin America, United States, Asia Pacific, Middle East, and Africa contributed to worldwide sales, with Europe, Latin America and the U.S. making up 40.1%, 30.9%, and 9.2% of worldwide sales respectively. In Asia Pacific, China/Hong Kong total sales decreased 3% due to foreign currency translation, with organic local-currency sales increasing 1%, while Japan had flat total and organic sales. In EMEA, West Europe total sales decreased 7% due to lost sales from divestitures and translation impacts, with organic sales flat. In Latin America/Canada, Mexico saw total sales increase 1% (5% organically), Canada had flat total sales with 5% organic growth offset by translation and divestitures, and Brazil saw total sales decrease 11% as organic growth of 5% was offset by translation. In 2018, foreign currency translation decreased sales by 2.3% overall, with decreases in Latin America/Canada, EMEA, and Asia Pacific, while selling prices increased 1.4% year-on-year, with strong growth in Latin America/Canada, EMEA, and the U.S., and lower price growth in Asia Pacific due to strong volume growth in electronics. For the full year, foreign currency translation increased sales by 0.2%, with gains in EMEA and Asia Pacific offset by decreases in Latin America/Canada, and selling prices increased 1.1% year-on-year, with strong growth in Latin America/Canada, EMEA, and the U.S., and slight price growth in Asia Pacific due to volume effects. In 2018, 3M generated $6.4 billion of operating cash flow, an increase of $199 million from 2017, following a $422 million decrease from 2016. In November 2018, 3M’s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $10 billion of its outstanding common stock, replacing the February 2016 program with no pre-established end date. In 2018, the Company purchased $4.9 billion of its own stock, compared to $2.1 billion in 2017 and $3.8 billion in 2016, and expected to purchase $2.0 billion to $4.0 billion in 2019. In February 2019, 3M declared a first-quarter 2019 dividend of $1.44 per share, a 6 percent increase, marking the 61st consecutive year of dividend increases. The Company has an AA- credit rating with a stable outlook from Standard & Poor’s and an A1 rating with a stable outlook from Moody’s Investors Service, and generates significant ongoing cash flow with proven access to capital markets. Raw material prices increased across most material markets worldwide in 2018, but the Company mitigated this through productivity projects, input management, reformulations, multi-sourcing, and strategic supplier relationships, successfully offsetting the headwinds and maintaining sufficient raw material supplies. 3M manages price risks through negotiated supply contracts, price protection agreements, and commodity price swaps. Globally, 3M’s pension and postretirement plans were 89 percent funded at year-end 2018, with the primary U.S. qualified pension plan at 96 percent funded and international plans at 89 percent; the U.S. non-qualified plan is not funded due to tax considerations. The primary U.S. qualified pension plan had a -0.5% asset return in 2018, with an expected long-term return of 7.00% for 2019, a year-end discount rate of 4.36% (up from 3.68% in 2017), which reduced the projected benefit obligation and increased the funded status by 2 percentage points due to a $200 million contribution. 3M expects to contribute $100 million to $200 million to its global defined benefit pension and postretirement plans in 2019, with no required minimum cash contribution for U.S. plans, and expects global defined benefit pension and postretirement expense to decrease by approximately $130 million pre-tax in 2019 compared to 2018. In February 2019, 3M completed the acquisition of the technology business of M*Modal, based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, for approximately $0.7 billion in cash (subject to adjustments) and the assumption of approximately $0.3 billion of M*Modal’s debt; M*Modal is a healthcare technology provider of cloud-based, conversational artificial intelligence-powered systems that help physicians capture and improve patient narratives, and the transaction will be reflected within 3M’s Health Care business. Net sales were flat year-on-year in 2017, with selling prices remaining flat, while in 2018, selling prices increased by 1.1 percent year-on-year. Cost of sales as a percent of sales increased in 2018 due to foreign currency effects and restructuring charges in the second and fourth quarters of 2018 in the Communication Markets Division, partially offset by selling price increases and the absence of 2017 footprint optimization charges. Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 14.7 percent in 2018 due to restructuring charges and the Minnesota NRD resolution charge, partially offset by the absence of 2017 optimization charges. Research, development and related expenses decreased $49 million in 2018 due to the divestiture of the Communication Markets Division, with R&D as a percent of sales at 5.6% in 2018, down from 5.9% in 2017 and 2016. In the first quarter of 2018, 3M divested personal safety product offerings and a polymer additives business, resulting in a $24 million gain, and divested an abrasives glass business resulting in a gain of less than $15 million; in June 2018, 3M completed the sale of its Communication Markets Division (annual sales of approximately $400 million) to Corning Incorporated, resulting in a $494 million gain, and in December 2018, sold the remaining telecommunications system integration services in Germany for a $15 million pre-tax gain, both reported within Electronics and Energy. Operating income margins declined 2.3 percentage points in 2018 compared to 2017, driven by the Minnesota NRD resolution charge, which reduced margins by 2.7 percentage points, while excluding that charge, margins increased 0.4 percentage points year-on-year. The decline was also due to higher defined benefit pension and postretirement service cost expenses, foreign exchange impacts, and acquisition/divestiture effects, while organic volume, productivity, and foreign exchange benefits partially offset the decline. The 2017 divestiture of the identity management business negatively impacted margins, while gains from divestitures and organic growth positively impacted them.

Operating income margins increased 0.4 percentage points year-on-year for full year 2018, compared to a 1.0 percentage point increase in 2017 when compared to the same period in 2016. The 2017 increase was driven by a gain from the May 2017 divestiture of the identity management business, higher organic local-currency sales growth and productivity, and benefits from raw material sourcing cost reductions, partially offset by actuarial adjustments to the respirator mask/asbestos liability accrual and higher defined benefit pension service cost expenses. Operating margins decreased in 2017 due to incremental strategic investments and charges related to 3M’s portfolio and supply chain optimization. Acquisitions and divestitures, including the October 2017 acquisition of Scott Safety and year-on-year divestiture gains (excluding identity management), benefited operating income margins in 2017. In 2018, operating income margins increased 1.3 percentage points in the Industrial business due to organic sales growth and portfolio actions, while in the Safety and Graphics business, margins decreased 7.9 percentage points primarily due to the 2017 gain from divestitures and the impact of the Scott Safety acquisition. The effective tax rate for 2018 was 23.4%, down from 35.5% in 2017, a decrease of 12.1 percentage points, primarily due to the enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) in December 2017, which resulted in a $762 million net tax expense in Q4 2017 and $176 million in measurement period adjustments in 2018 related to the transition tax on previously unremitted earnings of non-U.S. subsidiaries. The TCJA reduced the U.S. federal corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%, introduced a global intangible low-taxed income (GILTI) provision, added foreign-derived intangible income (FDII) incentives, changed U.S. tax implications of dividends, limited executive compensation deductibility, and repealed the domestic production activity deduction. The Company estimates its effective tax rate for 2019 will be approximately 20 to 22 percent. Currency effects, including hedging impacts, decreased pre-tax income by $42 million in 2018 and $111 million in 2017, with derivative and transaction gains and losses reducing pre-tax income by $92 million and $152 million, respectively. In 2018, Corporate and Unallocated operating expenses increased by $1.1 billion year-on-year, including a $897 million Minnesota NRD resolution in Q1 2018, restructuring charges of $105 million in Q2 and $22 million in Q4, and increased pension and postretirement service cost allocations. In 2017, Corporate and Unallocated expenses increased by $74 million, including $58 million in actuarial adjustments to the respirator mask/asbestos liability accrual and a $30 million increase in pension and postretirement service cost allocations. The Industrial business had sales of $12.267 billion in 2018, up 3.4% in U.S. dollars, with organic local-currency sales growth of 3.2%, divestitures reducing sales by 0.1%, and translation increasing sales by 0.3%. In 2017, Industrial sales were $11.866 billion, up 5.8%, with organic growth of 5.8%, divestitures reducing sales by 0.5%, and translation increasing sales by 0.5%. The Safety and Graphics business had sales of $6.827 billion in 2018, up 9.5%, with organic growth of 5.1%, acquisitions adding 7.3%, divestitures reducing sales by 3.1%, and translation increasing sales by 0.2%. In 2017, sales were $6.235 billion, up 4.8%, with organic growth of 6.3%, divestitures reducing sales by 4.2%, and translation increasing sales by 0.5%. Key divestitures included the sale of the Polyfoam business in January 2016, temporary protective films in October 2016, polymer additives compounding in Q1 2018, and abrasives glass products in May 2018. Key divestitures in 2017 included the identity management business, tolling and automated license/number plate business, and electronic monitoring business. The acquisition of Scott Safety in October 2017 contributed to sales growth in Safety and Graphics in 2018. 3M adopted ASU No. 2017-07 effective January 1, 2018, which reclassified pension and postretirement net periodic benefit cost components (except service cost) to other expense (income), net. The business segments are Industrial, Safety and Graphics, Health Care, Electronics and Energy, and Consumer, with Corporate and Unallocated including miscellaneous items, contract manufacturing, and restructuring charges.

In 2018, 3M reported sales in Safety and Graphics totaling $6.2 billion, up 4.8 percent in U.S. dollars, with organic local-currency sales increasing 6.3 percent, acquisitions adding 2.2 percent, divestitures reducing sales by 4.2 percent, and foreign currency translation boosting sales by 0.5 percent. Sales growth was led by personal safety and roofing granules, while transportation safety showed positive growth and the commercial solutions business was flat. ASC 715 requires employers to recognize the underfunded or overfunded status of a defined benefit pension or postretirement plan as an asset or liability in the statement of financial position and to recognize changes in funded status in the year of change through accumulated other comprehensive income, a component of stockholders’ equity. Pension benefits are primarily based on each participant’s years of service, compensation, and age at retirement or termination. The benefit obligation represents the present value of future benefits employees are entitled to for services already rendered as of the measurement date. The Company measures this present value by projecting benefit payment cash flows for each future period and discounting them back to December 31 using yields from a portfolio of high-quality, fixed-income debt instruments that would produce cash flows sufficient in timing and amount to settle projected future benefits. Service cost and interest cost are measured separately using the spot yield curve approach applied to each corresponding obligation. Service costs are determined using duration-specific spot rates applied to service cost cash flows, and interest cost is calculated by applying duration-specific spot rates to year-by-year projected benefit payments. The spot yield curve approach does not affect the total benefit obligation because changes in service and interest costs offset in actuarial gains and losses recorded in other comprehensive income. Stock-based compensation: The Company recognizes compensation expense for its stock-based compensation programs, which include stock options, restricted stock, restricted stock units (RSUs), performance shares, and the General Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (GESPP). Under applicable accounting standards, the fair value of share-based compensation is determined at the grant date and the related expense is recorded over the period in which the share-based compensation vests. However, with respect to income taxes, the related deduction from taxes payable is based on the award’s intrinsic value at the time of exercise (for an option) or on the fair value upon vesting of the award (for RSUs), which can be either greater (creating an excess tax benefit) or less (creating a tax deficiency) than the deferred tax benefit recognized as compensation cost. These excess tax benefits/deficiencies are recognized as income tax benefit/expense in the statement of income and, within the statement of cash flows, are classified in operating activities in the same manner as other cash flows related to income taxes. The extent of excess tax benefits/deficiencies is subject to variation in 3M stock price and timing/extent of RSU vestings and employee stock option exercises.  
Comprehensive income: Total comprehensive income and the components of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) are presented in the Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income and the Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity. Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) is composed of foreign currency translation effects (including hedges of net investments in international companies), defined benefit pension and postretirement plan adjustments, unrealized gains and losses on available-for-sale debt and equity securities, and unrealized gains and losses on cash flow hedging instruments.  
Derivatives and hedging activities: All derivative instruments within the scope of ASC 815, Derivatives and Hedging, are recorded on the balance sheet at fair value. The Company uses interest rate swaps, currency and commodity price swaps, and foreign currency forward and option contracts to manage risks generally associated with foreign exchange rate, interest rate and commodity market volatility. All hedging instruments that qualify for hedge accounting are designated and effective as hedges, in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. If the underlying hedged transaction ceases to exist, all changes in fair value of the related derivatives that have not been settled are recognized in current earnings. Instruments that do not qualify for hedge accounting are marked to market with changes recognized in current earnings. Cash flows from derivative instruments are classified in the statement of cash flows in the same category as the cash flows from the items subject to designated hedge or undesignated (economic) hedge relationships. The Company does not hold or issue derivative financial instruments for trading purposes and is not a party to leveraged derivatives.  
Credit risk: The Company is exposed to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by counterparties in interest rate swaps, currency swaps, commodity price swaps, and forward and option contracts. Entities can no longer recognize unrealized holding gains and losses on available-for-sale equity securities in other comprehensive income (OCI), and they are no longer permitted to use the cost method for equity securities without readily determinable fair values. Instead, for such investments not qualifying for the net asset value practical expedient, entities may elect a practicability exception to measure the investment at cost less impairment plus or minus observable price changes in orderly transactions. The ASU also introduces an incremental recognition and disclosure requirement for financial liabilities where the fair value option (FVO) has been elected, mandating that the portion of fair value changes attributable to instrument-specific credit risk be separately presented in OCI, while the rest remains in earnings—this does not apply to derivative instruments measured at fair value with changes recognized in current earnings. For 3M, this standard became effective beginning January 1, 2018, with an immaterial cumulative-effect adjustment to beginning retained earnings, except for the guidance on equity securities without readily determinable fair values, which is applied prospectively.
